stemMd: Two proteins have the same amino-acid composition but different amino-acid sequences. Which level of structure necessarily differs?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Total number of peptide bonds in equal-length chains

explanationMd: Primary structure is the ordered sequence of residues, not merely their counts. Identical composition therefore does not guarantee identical primary structure or folding.

distractorRationale.a: Equal chain lengths give equal peptide-bond counts.
distractorRationale.b: Both ordinary polypeptide chains have amino termini.
